source_note: Hobby 'TT' gearmotors, the drive of OpenBot and most robot-car kits. Figures are the seller's own technical details; a TT motor has no maker datasheet. The stall current is the seller's bench measurement of one motor (it warns motors vary), not a rating; continuous and peak torque limits are not published, so those checks report unknown, never pass.

families.quote: Rated Voltage: 3~6V Continuous No-Load Current: 150mA +/- 10% Min. Operating Speed (6V): 200+/- 10% RPM Stall Torque (6V): 0.8kg.cm Gear Ratio: 1:48 Weight: 30.6g
families.stall_current_basis: Adafruit, same page: 'We grabbed one motor ... At 6VDC we measured 160mA @ 250 RPM no-load, and 1.5 Amps when stalled' (3 V: 1.1 A, 4.5 V: 1.2 A). One sample on a bench supply; 'There will be variation from motor to motor'.
families.quote_measured: At 3VDC we measured 150mA @ 120 RPM no-load, and 1.1 Amps when stalled. At 4.5VDC we measured 155mA @ 185 RPM no-load, and 1.2 Amps when stalled At 6VDC we measured 160mA @ 250 RPM no-load, and 1.5 Amps when stalled.
